screen: Company — SWDY (route `company`, rendered under `sc-if p.isCompany`, lines 296–475 of `/Users/barbary/Documents/Codex/2026-07-13/fin/thebarbarianproject/design/The Barbarian.dc.html`)
summary: A single-company research screen for an EGX listing: a dark quote header carrying a 56-tick arc gauge for the 52-week range, then a five-way segmented tab row that swaps the body between Overview (stat tiles + revenue bar chart + research cards + discussion preview), Financials (a horizontally scrolling annual table with a frozen line-item column), Research, Filings and Discussion. sections.description: A 56-blade half-circle tick gauge spanning -90deg to +90deg. Blades below the value ratio are ember, the rest are dim; each lit blade animates in with a 9ms-per-index stagger. The big number and an uppercase caption sit inside the arc; the low and high bounds sit at the bottom corners. Centred in the card.

Blade head (child, sits at rod top): width:2px; height:31px; border-radius:1px. Lit: background:#E8621C; animation:bTick 220ms ease-out both; animation-delay:(i*9)ms (last lit blade starts at 378ms; total ≈598ms). Dim: background:rgba(245,241,236,0.16), no animation. @keyframes bTick{from{background:rgba(245,241,236,0.16)}to{background:#E8621C}}. Centre text block: position:absolute; left:0; right:0; bottom:46px; text-align:center. Big value: font:200 43px/1 Outfit,sans-serif (43 = round(214*0.2)); letter-spacing:-0.03em (= -1.29px); color:#F5F1EC; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums. sections.name: Segmented tab row — 5 tabs (lines 322-328, styles at lines 865-866)

interactions: Screen entry: the whole route column plays `bRise` — 240ms ease-out, opacity 0→1 with translateY(4px)→0.

52-week gauge reveal: each of the 43 lit blades plays `bTick` (background rgba(245,241,236,0.16) → #E8621C) for 220ms ease-out with fill-mode `both`, staggered by index * 9ms. Blade 0 starts at 0ms, blade 42 starts at 378ms, so the sweep completes at ~598ms. Unlit blades 43–55 are static and do not animate. The sweep runs left→right (angle -90° → +90°).

Segmented tab row: tap any of the five pills sets state.seg to 'ovr' | 'fin' | 'res' | 'dis' | 'disq'. Transition `all 220ms ease-out` on background, box-shadow and color — the pill cross-fades from rgba(27,25,23,.05)/#7A736D to #FFFFFF/#1B1917 with the shadow fading in. Body panels swap instantly (they are sc-if branches with no transition of their own). Default segment on mount is 'ovr'.
Back button (‹): calls p.back → `this.go(i, s.prev || fallback)` where fallback is derived from the current nav ('pit'→pit, 'you'→you, 'market'→market, else home). No press animation specified.
Overflow (···): rendered but has NO onClick handler in the design. Behaviour is unspecified.

Dark research card + light research card (Overview) and all three Research-tab cards: tap → p.goReader (route 'reader', nav unchanged). Press feedback: `transition:transform 220ms ease-out` with active state `transform:scale(0.98)`.
'See all' (Discussion section header): tap → p.goPit (route 'pit', nav set to 'pit' — so the bottom nav pill slides to the third slot).

Overview discussion preview card and every Discussion-tab post card: tap → p.goPost (route 'post', nav unchanged). These have `cursor:pointer` but NO scale-active transform — they do not shrink on press, unlike the research cards.

Financials table: horizontal scroll only (overflow-x:auto, scrollbar hidden). The header row is sticky to the top of that scroll area and the 132px 'Line item' column is sticky to the left, so the year headers slide under a frozen label column. Track min-width is 420px against a ~318px viewport, so ~102px of horizontal travel exists at minimum.
Filing rows: no onClick — the Filings list is read-only in this design.

Bottom nav: the four tabs remain tappable from this screen (goHome / goMarket / goPit / goYou). The active pill slides via `bPill` 320ms cubic-bezier(.32,1.2,.44,1) — a slight overshoot spring. On the Company screen the Market slot is lit by default (nav seeded to 'market').
No pull-to-refresh, no skeleton/loading state, no error state is specified for this screen (those live on the separate STATES screen at lines 696-751, which I did not read for this task).
flutterNotes:
SCAFFOLD. One `CustomScrollView`/`SingleChildScrollView` with padding EdgeInsets.fromLTRB(16, 54, 16, 124) inside a Stack; status bar and bottom nav are Positioned siblings above it. Body is a Column with 20px gaps (use a spaced Column helper, not Wrap).

FONTS. Register `Outfit` at w200/w300/w400/w500 and `IBM Plex Sans Arabic` at w300/w400/w500. Every numeric run in the design sets `font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums` → add `fontFeatures: [FontFeature.tabularFigures()]` to those TextStyles (price, gauge value, header stats, stat tile values/deltas, chart axis labels, all table cells, filing dates, post comment counts, status bar time). CSS line-heights are unitless multipliers, so map `font:300 22px/1.15` to `fontSize:22, height:1.15`. CSS letter-spacing is in `em`; Flutter wants logical px — the conversions are pre-computed in the tokens/sections above (e.g. .12em @10px = 1.2, -0.03em @43px = -1.29). CSS `text-transform:uppercase` is not a Flutter property: uppercase the strings yourself at render time and keep the original casing in the data layer (matters for Arabic later, where uppercasing is a no-op and the design's `letter-spacing` on Arabic will look wrong — see RTL).

THE ARC GAUGE — the one genuinely tricky widget. Do NOT reach for a charting package. It is 56 `Transform.rotate` children in a `Stack`, or (better) a single `CustomPainter`. Exact reproduction, size=214:
  • SizedBox(width: 214, height: 153)  // height = size/2 + 46
  • pivot is at (width/2, height - 22) = (107, 131)
  • blade i (0..55): angle = (-90 + i/55 * 180) degrees, converted to radians
  • the blade head is a 2x31 rounded rect (radius 1) whose FAR end is 107px from the pivot — i.e. it occupies radius 76..107 along the ray
  • lit if i < 43 (filled = round(56 * clamp((65.42-41.1)/(72.8-41.1))) = round(56*0.76719) = 43)
  • lit colour #E8621C, unlit rgba(245,241,236,0.16)
Animate with one AnimationController of ~598ms driving a value 0..1; for blade i use `Interval(i*9/598, (i*9+220)/598, curve: Curves.easeOut)` and lerp the colour from the unlit tone to #E8621C. CSS `ease-out` ≈ `Curves.easeOut` (cubic-bezier(0,0,.58,1)) — `Curves.easeOutCubic` is noticeably snappier, prefer `Curves.easeOut`. Only lit blades animate. The centre value/caption are a Positioned(bottom: 46, left: 0, right: 0) centred Column; lo/hi are Positioned(bottom: 0, left/right: 2). Keep the gauge generic — parameterise on {size, value, min, max, big, caption, lo, hi} because a second config (`dialVerdict`, size 230, 0–100, big '72', caption 'Cash', lo 'Trash', hi 'Cash') exists in the seed data for another screen.

SHADOWS. `0 8px 24px rgba(27,25,23,.06)` → BoxShadow(color: Color(0x0F1B1917), offset: Offset(0,8), blurRadius: 24). Note CSS blur-radius and Flutter blurRadius are not identical (CSS blur = 2σ, Flutter blurRadius ≈ 2σ as well for BlurStyle.normal, so a 1:1 copy is close but visually slightly tighter in Flutter) — if it reads too crisp, multiply blurRadius by ~1.15 rather than inventing new values.

INSET SHADOWS ARE HAIRLINES. Flutter has no inset box-shadow. `inset 0 -1px 0 rgba(27,25,23,.08)` on a table/filing row → `Border(bottom: BorderSide(color: Color(0x141B1917), width: 1))` (or a 1px Container). `inset 0 1px 0 rgba(245,241,236,.08)` on the header stat strip → a top border. `inset 0 0 0 1px <c>` on the verdict pill and kind chip → `Border.all(color: c, width: 1)` with NO fill. IMPORTANT: the filings list applies the bottom hairline to every row including the last, so the final row keeps its rule 4px above the card edge — reproduce that, do not "fix" it.

FROZEN-COLUMN TABLE. The financials table needs a 132px pinned label column + a horizontally scrollable 4-column body, with the header row pinned vertically. Cleanest Flutter shape: an outer Row of [fixed 132px Column of label cells] + [Expanded(SingleChildScrollView(scrollDirection: Axis.horizontal, child: Column of Rows))], with the header rendered as the first item of each side so the two stay in lockstep. Track min-width 420px; row height exactly 44px; numeric cells right-aligned with 16px trailing padding. KNOWN DEFECT to raise with design: the FY25 *header* cell uses padding-right 20px while its *body* cells use 16px, so the last column's header is 4px out of alignment with its values. Pick one (16px) unless design says otherwise.

CHART. Eight bars, `Row(crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.end)` inside a SizedBox(height: 128), each `Expanded` wrapping a Container with `height: 128 * pct` and BorderRadius.circular(10) — heights are 48.64 / 56.32 / 52.48 / 66.56 / 79.36 / 93.44 / 113.92 / 128.0. Gap 8px (SizedBox between, or Row with spacing). Bars 1–7 use Color(0x1A1B1917), bar 8 uses #1B1917; the axis label row mirrors the same flex/gap so labels line up under bars. There are no bar values, no axis line, no gridlines, no tooltip in the design — do not add any.

NO-INVENT LIST (product rules). Nothing on this screen says BUY, SELL, TARGET, STOP or EXPECTED RETURN, and nothing may be added. The only judgement token is the verdict pill "Verdict 72 · Cash" — it is a score plus a word, and it must stay ember-outlined text, never a coloured dot alone. Every ▲/▼ delta already pairs a glyph with the colour; keep both (and give each a semantics label like "up 11.3 percent" — the bare glyph is not announced usefully by TalkBack/VoiceOver). Segmented tab state is carried by fill + shadow + icon tint AND the persistent text label, which satisfies the never-colour-alone rule; do not drop the labels when localising. The staleness rule is satisfied by "Prices delayed 15 minutes" (#6E6862, 300 10px/1.4) directly under the quote block and by "EGP millions · audited · scroll for more years" + "Source: company filings via EGX disclosures" on the financials card — these strings are load-bearing compliance copy, not decoration; never hide them behind a tap.

DATA-LAYER CAVEATS FOR THE ENGINEER.
  • The Overview "Barbarian research" cards and the Overview discussion preview are HARDCODED in the markup, not bound to the `research`/`posts` arrays. The Research tab and Discussion tab ARE bound. Model them as the same card widget with an explicit model on both paths.
  • The Research tab and Discussion tab render the GLOBAL feeds unfiltered — a banking sector piece and an ORAS post appear on the SWDY company screen. That is almost certainly a prototype shortcut, not intent; assume they should be filtered by ticker and confirm with design.
  • Meta strings differ between the two research surfaces: Overview says "14 min read · 4 Aug", the Research tab says "14 min · 4 Aug". Don't derive one from the other; keep them as separate format strings until design picks one.
  • Stat tile `Net debt 12.9 bn ▲ 8.8%` is flagged `up:true` (green, up arrow), but the financials table shows net debt FALLING 14,120 → 12,880 (which is -8.8%). So `up`/`down` in the seed data means "good/bad", not "increased/decreased". Model the flag as a sentiment enum (favourable / unfavourable) plus a separate direction, or you will render the arrow backwards the first time real data arrives.
  • State keys are misleadingly named: `dis`/`disOn` drives the tab LABELLED **Filings**, and `disq`/`disqOn` drives **Discussion**. Rename to `filings`/`discussion` in Flutter.
  • The tab set is a five-value enum with 'ovr' as the default; only one panel is mounted at a time (sc-if, not a hidden-but-alive tab view), so an IndexedStack that preserves scroll offsets would be a behaviour change — use a plain switch unless you want that.

RTL / ARABIC — direction-sensitive items on this screen:
  1. Back chevron '‹' must flip to '›' in RTL. Use `Icons.chevron_left` with `matchTextDirection`/`Directionality`-aware icon, not a literal glyph.
  2. The gauge is the biggest risk. `lo` is hard-positioned left and `hi` right, and the fill sweeps left→right. A numeric range gauge conventionally stays LTR even in Arabic UI — wrap the gauge in `Directionality(textDirection: TextDirection.ltr)` so low stays at the visual left, and confirm with design rather than mirroring it by default. Mirroring would also reverse the tick stagger, which reads wrong.
  3. `▲ 1.16 (1.80%)` and `▲ 11.3%` mix a symbol, Latin digits and parentheses — in an RTL paragraph these will reorder without bidi isolation. Emit them inside an LRI/PDI isolate (or a `Directionality(ltr)` inline span) so the arrow stays left of the number and the parens don't swap.
  4. The financials table's frozen column is pinned LEFT and numerics are `justify-content:flex-end`. In RTL the label column should pin to the RIGHT and the numeric columns keep their numbers aligned toward the label column. Build with logical start/end (Flutter's Row + TextDirection does this for free) rather than hard left/right, but force the digit runs themselves to LTR.
  5. The revenue chart runs oldest→newest left→right. In RTL, mirroring is the correct default for a time axis in Arabic layouts — but it must mirror the bars AND the axis labels together, and the inked "current year" bar must stay on the newest end.
  6. `letter-spacing` on uppercase Latin kickers (.12em–.16em) must be dropped for Arabic — letter-spacing breaks Arabic joining. Gate it on the active locale/script.
  7. The Arabic company name already carries `dir="rtl"` inside an otherwise-LTR block — in Flutter wrap it in `Directionality(textDirection: TextDirection.rtl)` and align it to the block's start, not hard-left.
  8. Text-overflow: the ticker (42px), the price (30px) and the identity row use `justify-content:space-between` with `gap:12px` and no ellipsis. A 6-char ticker or a 5-digit price (ORAS is 412.10 in the same dataset) will collide. Add `Flexible` + `FittedBox(fit: BoxFit.scaleDown)` on the price, and ellipsis on the Arabic name.
  9. Segmented pills are fixed 56px wide with a 9px label. "Discussion" barely fits in English; Arabic and German will overflow. Either allow the label to wrap to two 9px lines inside the 62px pill or let the pill grow — confirm with design which.

VALUES I DID NOT READ, so do not assume: hover/focus/pressed styling beyond the two `style-active:transform:scale(0.98)` cases; any pressed state for the segmented pills, the back/overflow buttons, the post cards or the filing rows; ripple/splash colours; the overflow menu contents; scroll physics or overscroll behaviour; safe-area insets (the design hardcodes 54px top / 124px bottom against a 390x844 shell); the empty/loading/error variants of any of these panels (they live on the separate STATES screen, lines 696-751, which was out of scope here).
